PRIMARY_SUPPORTED_CLAIM: The compact 14-D axial-radial representation provides reproducible incremental garment-category predictive utility beyond the frozen 135-D morphology representation under garment-identity-disjoint validation.
SECONDARY_SUPPORTED_CLAIM: Most of the direct incremental predictive gain is carried by the radial component of the representation.
ROBUSTNESS_SUPPORTED_CLAIM: The observed increment is robust to garment-identity cluster resampling and to repeated category-balanced grouped partitions.
ALIGNMENT_NOT_SUPPORTED: The data do not support the claim that the predictive increment depends on exact garment-level correspondence between morphology and axial-radial features.
ALIGNMENT_INTERPRETATION: Category-preserving identity misalignment reproduced or exceeded the correctly aligned gain, indicating that category-level axial-radial distributional structure is sufficient to explain the tested downstream improvement.
NOT_CLAIMED: information-theoretic independence of morphology and axial-radial geometry
causal contribution of radial or axial geometry
superiority to all classical or learned shape representations
